title: Adverbs of Manner
theoryHTML:
1. What is an Adverb of Manner?

Adjectives describe nouns (things or people), but Adverbs of Manner describe verbs (actions). They tell us HOW an action is done.

Adjective: Pau is a quick runner. (Describes Pau)
Adverb: Pau runs quickly. (Describes HOW he runs)

2. The General Rule (+ly)

For most words, we just add -ly at the end of the adjective.

  • slow ➔ slowly
  • quick ➔ quickly
  • bad ➔ badly
  • careful ➔ carefully
  • happy ➔ happily (change 'y' to 'i')
The teacher speaks slowly so we can understand.
He finished the Minecraft house easily.

3. Irregular Adverbs (The Rebels!) 🚨

Some adverbs don't follow the rules. You must memorize these because they are very common in English!

  • good ➔ well (NEVER say 'goodly')
  • fast ➔ fast (NEVER say 'fastly')
  • hard ➔ hard (NEVER say 'hardly' when you mean 'with effort')
  • late ➔ late (NEVER say 'lately' when you mean 'not on time')
He plays tennis very well. (Not 'very good')
The sports car goes very fast.
She trains very hard for the tournament.

questions.text: My brother plays the guitar very ___.
questions.explanation: We need an adverb to describe HOW he plays. The adverb of 'good' is the irregular word 'well'.

questions.text: The turtle walks very ___.
questions.explanation: We add '-ly' to the adjective 'slow' to make the adverb 'slowly'.

questions.text: You must run ___ if you want to win the race.
questions.explanation: 'Fast' is an irregular adverb. It does NOT take '-ly'. 'Fastly' doesn't exist in English!

questions.text: Please, speak ___. The baby is sleeping.
questions.explanation: We add '-ly' to 'quiet' to describe how you should speak: 'quietly'.

questions.text: I did very ___ in my math exam. I got a 3 out of 10.
questions.explanation: To describe the verb 'did', we use the adverb 'badly'.

questions.text: Link fights ___ against the monsters in Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom.
questions.explanation: We add '-ly' to 'brave'. It describes how he fights.

questions.text: She studies very ___ to get good grades.
questions.explanation: 'Hard' is an irregular adverb that stays exactly the same as the adjective. ('Hardly' means 'almost nothing', which is different!).

questions.text: The dog was eating its food ___ because it was very hungry.
questions.explanation: We add '-ly' to the adjective 'quick' to form the adverb 'quickly'.

questions.text: I can ___ lift this box, it's very light.
questions.explanation: When an adjective ends in 'y' (easy), we change the 'y' to 'i' and add '-ly': 'easily'.

questions.text: The children are playing ___ in the garden.
questions.explanation: Like 'easy', 'happy' ends in 'y'. Change it to 'i' and add '-ly': 'happily'.

questions.text: He woke up ___ and missed the school bus.
questions.explanation: 'Late' is an irregular adverb that doesn't change. ('Lately' means 'recently').

questions.text: You speak English very ___! Where did you learn it?
questions.explanation: You are describing HOW someone speaks (the verb). The adverb of 'good' is 'well'.

questions.text: Please write ___, I can't read your letters.
questions.explanation: We add '-ly' to 'clear' to describe how the person should write.

questions.text: The teacher looked at me ___ because I didn't do my homework.
questions.explanation: 'Angry' ends in 'y', so it becomes 'angrily'.

questions.text: The car crashed because he was driving ___.
questions.explanation: We add '-ly' to 'dangerous' to describe how he was driving.

questions.text: Don't drive so ___! The speed limit is 50 km/h.
questions.explanation: Remember the irregular rule: 'fast' is both an adjective and an adverb. 'Fastly' does not exist.

questions.text: We won the basketball match ___! The score was 80-20.
questions.explanation: We use the adverb 'easily' to describe how we won.

questions.text: You need to kick the ball ___ to score a goal from here.
questions.explanation: To describe kicking with a lot of force, we use 'hard'. It is an irregular adverb.

questions.text: He opened the door ___ because it was broken.
questions.explanation: We add '-ly' to 'careful'. Since careful already has an 'L', it becomes 'carefully' with double L.

questions.text: The dog barks ___ when a stranger comes to the house.
questions.explanation: We add '-ly' to the adjective 'loud' to make the adverb 'loudly'.

questions.text: She dances ___. She should go to a talent show!
questions.explanation: We add '-ly' to 'beautiful'. It gets a double L: 'beautifully'.

questions.text: My grandmother drives very ___.
questions.explanation: We use the adverb 'carefully' to describe the action of driving.

questions.text: I answered all the questions ___ and got a 10/10.
questions.explanation: We add '-ly' to 'perfect' to describe how the questions were answered.

questions.text: It is raining ___. We can't go to the park.
questions.explanation: 'Heavy' ends in 'y', so we change it to 'i' and add '-ly': 'heavily'.

questions.text: He is a ___ student, but he behaves ___ in class.
questions.explanation: Tricky one! 'Good' is an adjective describing the noun 'student'. 'Badly' is the adverb describing the verb 'behaves'.
